verdict_text: NO. The plan never deletes the source `lora::...lora_A.weight` / `lora_B.weight` tensors after the `matmul` step — only the intermediate `delta` tensors are deleted via `delete: { target: 'model::...delta(_t)?' }`. Since `matmul` (unlike the trailing-underscore `scale_`/`cast_`/`add_` in-place transforms) does not consume its inputs, the 32 adapter tensors remain in the final tensor set and would be written into the sharded output, violating "No adapter tensor... appears in the output" and the "output has exactly 244 tensors" requirement (actual would be 276). Both the `not: { exists: 'model::.*lora_.*' } }` and `count: { of: 'model::.*', is: 244 } }` asserts are scoped only to the `model::` provider namespace, so they never inspect the still-present `lora::` tensors and would pass despite the defect — meaning the "Required checks" are not actually enforced as specified.
